How it was scored

  • Scanned with OpenSCAP in the image build on 2026-10-19 09:48 UTC.
  • Content: SCAP Security Guide 0.1.82, profile “CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Benchmark for Level 2 - Server” (xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_cis), as published.
  • Score = rules passed ÷ (rules passed + rules failed). Every rule listed under Exemptions failed in the scan and counts as a failure in the score. Not-applicable and not-checked rules are not scored.
  • AlmaLinux is scored with the SCAP Security Guide content for Red Hat Enterprise Linux, so the checks that only Red Hat Enterprise Linux can pass appear as exemptions below.
  • The build's OpenSCAP gate was enforced: floor 90%, and no failing rule without a documented exemption.

An OpenSCAP score measures this image against SSG content. It is not a certification, authorization or accreditation, and it is not an assessment of your system.

Exemptions (4)

Each rule below fails in the image for the reason given, and the last column is what you do to meet it on your instance. The reasons and actions come from the build record (this record is not covered by the bundle's signature).

RuleCategoryWhy it fails in the imageWhat you do
ensure_root_password_configured
Ensure Authentication Required for Single User Mode		AWS Marketplace policy: you complete it after launchAWS Marketplace policy prohibits meeting this rule in an AMI: "AMI must not contain hardcoded secrets such as system user and service passwords (including hashed passwords)" and "Password-based authentication for instance services is prohibited. This applies even if the password is generated, reset, or defined by the user at launch"; Linux AMIs "must allow users to get fully privileged access (for example, to allow sudo access)" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/product-and-ami-policies.html). The rule needs a boot loader or root password hash in the image, or a sudo password for the key-only default user.After launch run sudo stigready-set-credentials (installed in the image): it sets your own GRUB superuser and password, root password and a sudo password for your admin user, and removes NOPASSWD, which meets this rule on your instance.

ensure_redhat_gpgkey_installed
Ensure Red Hat GPG Key Installed		Check names Red Hat: cannot apply to this distributionThe check passes only when the OS is RHEL and Red Hat's own signing keys are installed (gpg-pubkey-fd431d51, the Red Hat release key, plus that release's auxiliary key). Rocky Linux and AlmaLinux sign their packages with their own release keys, so no derivative image can carry Red Hat's key honestly. What the rule protects -- packages are only installed when their signature verifies against the distribution's key -- is still enforced and scored on these images by ensure_gpgcheck_globally_activated and ensure_gpgcheck_never_disabled (and ensure_gpgcheck_local_packages on STIG), which pass.None. The distribution's own key (RPM-GPG-KEY-Rocky-N or RPM-GPG-KEY-AlmaLinux-N) is installed and gpgcheck is on for every repository. If your accreditation requires Red Hat-signed packages, use the RHEL image.
